lines: Wavetable oscillator with 70 tables of 256 single-cycle waveforms, three waveshaping modifiers in series, an additive engine layering the waveform at harmonic multiples, and eight-voice unison
Chooses which of the 256 single-cycle waveforms in the table is played, sweeping the shape from one end of the table to the other
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the position input jack; centred, none of it reaches POS, and at either end 10V covers the whole of the POS knob's travel
Mixes noise in with the oscillator waveform
Sets how many detuned copies of the waveform sound at once, one to eight
Sets how far the unison voices are detuned from one another
Sets how widely the unison voices are spread across the two outputs
Shifts the pitch in whole octaves, -3 to +3
Shifts the pitch in semitones, -11 to +11
Shifts the pitch by up to half a semitone either way, read out in cents
Sets the output level
Sets how far the first of the three modifiers reshapes the waveform, or the value of that modifier's own main setting
Sets how far the second of the three modifiers reshapes the waveform, working on what the first one has already done
Sets how far the third of the three modifiers reshapes the waveform, working on what the first two have already done
Switches the first modifier to reshape the waveform after the additive engine rather than before it
Switches the second modifier to reshape the waveform after the additive engine rather than before it
Switches the third modifier to reshape the waveform after the additive engine rather than before it
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the MOD 1 input jack; centred, none of it reaches the MOD 1 amount knob, and at either end 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the MOD 2 input jack; centred, none of it reaches the MOD 2 amount knob, and at either end 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the MOD 3 input jack; centred, none of it reaches the MOD 3 amount knob, and at either end 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
Scales the voltage at the FM jack before it modulates the oscillator frequency
Moves the POS knob by the voltage here, scaled by the POS trimmer
Moves the MOD 1 amount knob by the voltage here, scaled by the MOD 1 trimmer
Moves the MOD 2 amount knob by the voltage here, scaled by the MOD 2 trimmer
Moves the MOD 3 amount knob by the voltage here, scaled by the MOD 3 trimmer
Sets the pitch at a volt per octave, 0V giving C4 at 261.63Hz; the number of channels patched here sets how many voices the module runs
Modulates the oscillator frequency, scaled by the FM trimmer
Moves the selection on from the wavetable chosen in the display, by about seven tables per volt, so 10V reaches the last of the 70
The left output; the unison spread places the detuned voices across this output and the right one
The right output; the unison spread places the detuned voices across this output and the left one
Note — clicking the waveform display opens the 70 wavetables, grouped as basic, PWM, digital, Exode, modern, sync, sine, VS waves and XTable
Note — the waveform display draws the waveform as it will sound, with the modifiers and the additive layering already applied
Note — clicking a MOD display picks that modifier's algorithm: off, or one of 25 shapers such as frequency modulation, phase distortion, ring modulation, hard sync, decimation, clipping and folding
Note — the harmonics display is edited by dragging its bars: a bar above the middle sets the level of the copy at that harmonic, one below it sets that copy's phase, and grey bars mark the octaves
Menu — Reset Harmonics clears the additive engine back to the fundamental alone
Blamsoft-XFXWave.notes: Blamsoft publish no source; the control map, the ranges and the CV scalings were read out of the installed 2.0.4 binary (XFXWaveModule::process). Input 1 is declared in the module but has no widget on the panel, so no click can reach it and it is left untagged. The unlabelled jack above the waveform display is input 7: process reads it as wavetable = menu choice + int(6.9v + 0.5), clamped to 0-69, and the panel draws a connector line from that jack to the display. V/Oct is input 5 and FM is input 6, which is the reverse of their left-to-right order on the panel; the polyphony channel count comes from input 5. Params 9, 10 and 11 are declared with no name and no widget. Each of the four trimmers maps its 0-1 position to -1 to +1 and multiplies the jack voltage by 0.1, so a fully open trimmer lets 10V cover the whole 0-1 range of the control it feeds; the sum is then clamped, so CV cannot push a control past its limits.
